_comment: ~/.claude/harness/config.json — machine/person-level defaults. Project config overrides per key. Every key shown here has a sensible built-in default; delete what you don't need.

terminal._app_options: auto | iterm2 | terminal | tmux — 'auto' picks iTerm2 if installed, else Terminal.app, else tmux
terminal._windows_note: role → window-group map. Groups become OS windows; sessions in a group become tabs. Two groups = the 'orchestrators in one screen, execution in the other' layout.

accounts._note: OPTIONAL — leave empty to use your normal claude login (the default; one account is fine). If you manage multiple Claude accounts (e.g. work vs personal via a switcher like cloak), set env_command to any command that PRINTS export-style env vars for the account the harness should use, e.g. "cloak switch --print-env work". The generated launchers eval it before starting claude and fail loudly (exit 9) if it breaks. No rotation, no headroom-chasing — one identity per role at most.

models.question: opus
models._note: '|' means OR: try left first, fall back automatically if the model is unavailable/restricted at boot. Aliases: fable, mythos, opus, sonnet, or full claude-* ids. haiku is rejected by policy. Sonnet is reserved for command validation and big-context summarization.

limits._note: Pause, don't stop: at/above pause_next_spawn_at% of the 5h window, NEW spawns wait for the reset (running sessions are never touched). weekly_pause_at (default 99 = near-exhaustion) makes a weekly-capped run WAIT on the weekly reset instead of thrashing; set null to disable weekly pausing. stop_at null = never hard-stop. on_unreadable: proceed|hold when the usage API can't be read.

session._permissions_options: bypass (--dangerously-skip-permissions, classic unattended) | auto | acceptEdits | dontAsk

guardrails._note: sonnet_validation: every spawn's generated launcher is sonnet-reviewed before the terminal opens (second net after the deterministic guards). sonnet_trust_check: if a 'trust this folder?' dialog appears, a sonnet confirms the folder is legitimately part of the run before the watch loop answers yes (the folder is already deterministically verified to be inside the project first). Password/sudo prompts are NEVER auto-answered — they are owner-gated. Both cost one small -p sonnet call when they fire.
